answer: At a jetty market for crystal and pigment, voting coupons accrue per token-day in escrow, not per account. The ledger records each deposit's amount and time once; splitting it among aliases preserves total token-days. Spending a coupon consumes its credit globally, so one balance cannot back several votes at once. A farm needs more capital locked for longer, paying financing and opportunity costs. This requires correct time accounting and no account bonuses. It stops free usernames creating influence, but old wealthy holders can dominate.
